gen-gf-gugi-gf-victor-mono: Victor Mono reads like typewriter text blown up a size, spaced loosely, with bowls that stop short of closing. Gugi sits over it as a bold display heading, tall in the lowercase, so the two feel like a shout followed by a careful whisper.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-viga: Viga reads plainly, its capitals barely taller than the letters beside them and every stroke free of hairlines or shadows. Gugi is best at making a bold, distinctive entrance, while Viga is best at staying out of its way.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-winky-sans: Winky Sans reads modern and low-key, with capitals that barely rise above the lowercase around them. Winky Sans would carry a long passage smoothly, leaving Gugi's bold, open-cut display letters to do the showing off.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-clash-grotesk: Clash Grotesk is friendly and uncluttered, with no thick-and-thin swing. Happy Monkey does best at bold, ruler-straight display lines with wide gaps in the e, while Clash Grotesk does best at quietly carrying the words.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-fs-familjen-grotesk: Familjen Grotesk brings a lively, tall lowercase and curves that stop short of closing, a clear step up from the heading. And Happy Monkey's ruler-straight strokes give the pair its strongest quality: one steady monoline against a livelier, taller companion.
gen-gf-goldman-gf-allerta: Wide, bold, and sure of itself, Goldman puts round forms like open parentheses up top. Allerta, a sans-serif with loose tracking and a prominent x-height, is the one to hold the text.
gen-gf-goldman-gf-alumni-sans-sc: Alumni Sans SC reads tight and contemporary, its lowercase looking oversized beside its capitals and its stems only slightly heavier than the hairlines. But Goldman's generous, widely set letters make the strongest quality here: a spacious heading against a compact, squeezed body.
